The **Bengal cat** is a breed of hybrid "Hybrid (biology)") cat created from crossbreeding an Asian leopard cat to domestic cats (*Prionailurus bengalensis* × *Felis catus*), especially the spotted tabby Egyptian Mau. Bengals have varying appearances. The breed is selectively bred and pedigree registered with most of the major cat registries. The breed's name derives from that of the Asian leopard cat (*Prionailurus bengalensis*), from which the Bengal cat was originally hybridised. The earliest mention of an Asian leopard cat × domestic cat hybrid was in 1889, when Harrison Weir wrote of them in *Our Cats and All About Them*. The Cat Fanciers' Association (CFA) accepted the Bengal in CFA's "Miscellaneous" in 2016, under the restrictions that "it must be F6 or later (6 generations removed from the Asian leopard cat or non-Bengal domestic cat ancestors)".

english_retrieval.snippet: Bengals are often considered to be quite talkative, but this is not necessarily true of every Bengal. There is a great deal of variation from one cat to the next, with some choosing to engage in frequent conversation and others preferring to keep their thoughts to themselves. Genetic testing has enabled Bengal breeders to screen cats for a number of heritable diseases that may occur in the breed and remove carrier cats from the breeding program. :   **GENERAL**: The Bengal is a medium to large cat with a sleek, muscular build. The tail is thick, with rounded tip, and carried lower than the back. Slightly small in proportion to body, not to be taken to extreme. Eye color independent of coat color, except in the Lynx Points, where Blue is the only acceptable color. A much lighter to white ground color on the whisker pads, chin, chest, belly, and inner legs, in contrast to the ground color of the flanks and back is desirable.
